reason: Generic syndrome umbrella has no shared organ or mechanism axis; assigning a specific organ would be unsupported.
Arterial occlusion defines cardiovascular disease. Brain infarction or lasting neurologic damage is not inherent; the broader parent's neurologic label need not apply.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining myopathy and ophthalmoplegia. Gastrointestinal dysmotility affects 2/5 (40%); neuropathy and hearing impairment each affect only 1/5.
Lipoadenoma describes epithelial tumour morphology without an anatomical site. Neither glandular epithelium nor admixed fat establishes a specific organ axis.
Acquired CJD is a transmissible prion infection causing destructive brain disease, supporting neurologic and infectious_immune primary axes.

Vascular and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome. Cleft palate and persistent abnormal skin scarring each occur in 30–79%, supporting gastrointestinal and dermatologic involvement; associated asthma is separate.
Autoimmune destruction of skin melanocytes establishes dermatologic and infectious_immune primary axes. Associated autoimmune diseases do not establish additional involvement.
Immune-mediated bowel inflammation defines this subtype. Separately diagnosed anemia and motor delay without established intrinsic neurologic damage do not warrant additional axes.

Limb absence and lung agenesis define this subtype; cleft palate affects 6/7, supporting gastrointestinal involvement. No defining neurologic disease is documented; pulmonary vein hypoplasia affects only 2/7.
Zinc absorption and transport disorders share a metabolic mechanism. Skin, bowel, neurologic and renal damage vary across subtypes and are not established across most of the umbrella.
